description: Width tiers for Visual Arts — Years 9–10
subject: Visual Arts

width_notes.minimum: The narrowest single task context that honestly meets the descriptor's command term. For Years 9–10, minimum is a sustained, documented act of making, investigating or evaluating with identifiable personal expression or critical reasoning.
width_notes.typical: Full descriptor scope — extended investigation, critical evaluation, personal style development and sophisticated curation across a range of contexts, artists and forms.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment through additional cultural contexts, genres, activist or political dimensions, interdisciplinary connections and community/public exhibition contexts. Adds new contexts, not higher difficulty.

AC9AVA10C01.minimum_width: Seek and respond to at least one piece of critical feedback on a work in progress; document how it affected a decision.
AC9AVA10C01.typical_width: Evaluate critical feedback from teachers and peers across multiple works in progress; track decisions using self-assessment and Viewpoints questions; experiment with structuring ideas in sketches, studies, maquettes or journal entries; document responses to feedback.
wider: Collaborate with an external agency (community group, organisation) to generate ideas for an artwork or design project for a curated exhibition or community event — evaluate feedback from a real audience beyond the classroom
Create a virtual or scale model of an exhibition of a researched artist — use feedback and evaluation to communicate understanding of the artist's intentions
Develop a structured peer review process for the class — design the feedback questions, facilitate the review, and document how the process improved works
elaborations: uncovering meaning, interpretations or reactions from audiences by seeking impressions without confirming or leading the audience towards intended responses
tracking success using self-assessment and reflection guided by questions based on Viewpoints in order to solve creative challenges
experimenting with and evaluating ways of structuring ideas in sketches, studies, maquettes, annotated digital images or journal entries

evaluating and responding to feedback on works in process from teachers and peers, in discussions or reviews, and documenting their decisions and responses in written, oral or multimedia, physical or digital journals/diaries
collaborating with other students, groups or agencies, such as community groups, to generate ideas for artworks on design or artistic projects for curated exhibitions or events

AC9AVA10C02.minimum_width: Select and manipulate at least two visual conventions, processes or materials to create an artwork that reflects personal expression and communicates an intended idea or perspective.
AC9AVA10C02.typical_width: Select and manipulate visual conventions, processes and materials across multiple works to express personal voice; plan and refine approaches through research and annotation; create artworks that represent, challenge or re-interpret ideas, perspectives and meanings; use creative problem-solving throughout.
wider: Create artworks in response to current global or local issues (sustainable futures, human rights, wellbeing) — research how other artists have addressed similar themes and develop a distinct personal approach

Investigate how visual arts practice can explore and represent personal experiences respectfully — use the practice to process and communicate ideas about self-awareness, emotional awareness or personal wellbeing
Create site-specific 3D work that demonstrates understanding of sculptural techniques, space and form — document how site conditions shaped material and conceptual choices
elaborations: creating artworks that realise the intentions and communicate ideas developed through their experimentation and planning
researching approaches to representing their ideas and interests in the world/subjects or concepts from a particular viewpoint or a range of viewpoints
recording and documenting their research into their subject using their own images or images from other sources, written annotations, and comments and evaluations
initiating their own ways of resolving ideas and concepts visually, using creative problem-solving throughout the process
creating their own artworks in response to a specific subject, theme or idea, using material, techniques and conventions in intentional, interpretative and personal ways
applying their knowledge and understanding of visual arts processes and materials to create artworks

AC9AVA10D01.minimum_width: Experiment with one medium or form in depth; investigate its technical processes and document discoveries using a journal or portfolio.
AC9AVA10D01.typical_width: Experiment with and document investigations of visual art processes, conventions and materials in a diary, portfolio or digital journal; interrogate multiple approaches to a topic using diverse media; investigate artists through their sketchbooks; annotate processes and use Viewpoints to deepen understanding.
wider: Develop an 'inspiration' journal of collections from everyday life (photographs, found objects, media experiments, thoughts) — use Viewpoints questions to identify emerging personal style preferences and values

Draw lines, shapes and arrows over photocopies of artworks to decode compositional techniques — use a coding system to show rule of thirds, movement, repetition and visual hierarchy; apply findings to your own work
Investigate how artists from different places (e.g. a country in the Asia region) discuss the influences on their work — reflect on how these accounts inform your own practice
elaborations: experimenting with the material properties of a medium or form and investigating/exploring, in depth, the technical processes associated with that form
interrogating multiple ways of approaching an activity; for example, using a diverse range of media to express different interpretations of the one topic
investigating a diverse selection of artists through their sketchbooks to uncover their practices, and find connections between their processes and the development of their personal expression
developing an 'inspiration' journal of collections from everyday life
documenting and evaluating their investigations of visual art processes, visual conventions and materials in a diary, portfolio or digital journal
drawing lines, shapes and arrows drawn over photocopies of artworks and using a code to demonstrate their understanding of the way the artist has composed the artwork

AC9AVA10D02.minimum_width: Investigate at least one influence (personal, cultural or contextual) on their own visual arts practice; reflect on how it has shaped a choice or direction.
AC9AVA10D02.typical_width: Reflect on the role of culture, family, personal experience and other artists as influences on their visual arts practice; investigate artists from diverse places and contexts; analyse how artists structure artworks to represent ideas; resolve choices as work progresses through informal review.
wider: Explore current issues of importance (global or local) as a starting point for artwork — research how artists address themes such as sustainable futures, wellbeing or human rights; reflect on your own position

Investigate how First Nations Australian artists use their practices to explore and represent personal and community experiences — reflect on what these approaches suggest about how you might represent your own experiences

Investigate artists from a different cultural context (e.g. a country in the Asia region) who discuss influences on their work — reflect on how understanding their contexts expands your own awareness of what can shape a practice
elaborations: investigating and reflecting on the role and influence of their own culture, family or personal experiences when developing ideas for artworks
investigating a diverse range of visual artists; for example, artists who live and work in a different place, such as a country in the Asia region
analysing and reflecting on the ways that artists have structured their artworks to represent ideas
reflecting on, evaluating and resolving their choices for representing their ideas as their work progresses
exploring current issues that are of importance to them, such as global or local issues, as a starting point for generating and reflecting on ideas for artworks
investigating the ways that artists use their visual arts practice to explore, examine, resolve or represent personal experiences and expressions

AC9AVA10E01.minimum_width: Investigate at least one artist from a different culture, time or place; analyse how their personal expression and context shape the work.
AC9AVA10E01.typical_width: Investigate ways that artists across cultures, times and places develop personal expression to represent, communicate and challenge ideas; research, analyse and evaluate multiple artists; compare approaches to portraiture, identity, freedom, social change or other themes; produce extended written, oral or multimedia accounts.
wider: Investigate how linear versus circular timelines shift meaning in art — examine this with reference to First Nations Australian ways of knowing, being and doing
Explore the development of a visual arts form over time (e.g. woodblock printing or photography) — consider the impact of globalisation, cultural practices and material discoveries
Select different critical viewpoints (formal, contextual, socio-political) to develop competing explanations of the same artwork — evaluate which viewpoint illuminates most and why
elaborations: analysing a selection of artworks that represent a point of view on the same or similar theme, story, historical event, place, time, use of a technique or materials
investigating how linear timelines, in contrast to circular timelines, can shift meaning in art with reference to First Nations Australian ways of knowing, being and doing
researching, analysing and evaluating the ways that artists from different times and places represent subject matter, themes or concepts
creating extended written, oral or multimedia accounts, such as essays, pod/vodcast, debate or reviews
selecting different critical viewpoints to develop explanations about artists' approaches and works
exploring the development of a visual arts form over time, considering the impact of globalisation, cultural practices, and new discoveries in materials and technologies

AC9AVA10E02.minimum_width: Investigate at least one First Nations Australian artist whose work celebrates or challenges Australian identity; analyse one way the work communicates a perspective or lived experience.
AC9AVA10E02.typical_width: Investigate ways that First Nations Australian artists celebrate and challenge multiple perspectives of Australian identity; analyse protest posters, street art, gallery works; examine activism, 'first contacts' histories and contemporary identity debates; compare and evaluate approaches by diverse First Nations artists and designers.
wider: Work with representatives of the First Nations Australian community to explore how local groups are caring for Country/Place — investigate how visual arts campaigns highlight environmental issues

Analyse how First Nations Australian artists use visual arts to present multiple ways of understanding 'first contacts' between First Nations Peoples and British or European colonisers — evaluate the role of art in community debate
Investigate how contemporary First Nations Australian designers are challenging concepts and histories of Australian identity in applied and commercial design contexts
elaborations: researching a diverse range of artworks or designs such as artworks in galleries, protest posters or street art in order to analyse how and why First Nations Australian artists have used visual communication as a tool to express activism for change
analysing the ways that First Nations Australian artists use their practices to challenge and inform community debate
comparing, analysing and evaluating ways that contemporary First Nations Australian artists and designers are exploring and challenging concepts and histories of Australia and Australian identity
exploring the ways that First Nations Australian visual artists use their practices to communicate ideas, messages and lived experiences to the broader community
understanding ways that the arts provide opportunities for First Nations Australian artists and designers to continue and develop their culture
investigating how First Nations Australian visual artists are caring for Country/Place, culture and people through the visual arts

AC9AVA10P01.minimum_width: Evaluate at least one exhibition and identify one curatorial decision that could inform how they present their own work.
AC9AVA10P01.typical_width: Evaluate art exhibits in physical or virtual galleries, museums or community sites; plan and curate exhibitions of own work; develop exhibition materials (didactic panels, artist/curatorial statements, advertising); visit and evaluate exhibitions to inform own curation; present documentation in written, oral or multimedia forms.
wider: Plan and curate a community installation or imagined exhibition of artworks by other artists — consider Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property rights as appropriate

Develop a complete set of exhibition materials for a class show — didactic panels, artist statements, branding, advertising and press statements — evaluating each element's effectiveness for the intended audience
Create a virtual or scale model of an exhibition of a researched artist — communicate your understanding of the artist's intentions through the spatial and editorial choices made
elaborations: investigating ways in which artworks are displayed and how artists and curators work together to create a visual narrative
selecting and presenting their own artworks for exhibitions in class, in the school or in the wider community

planning and curating exhibitions of their own work, community installations, projects or imagined exhibitions of artworks by other artists, considering, as appropriate, Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property rights
developing material to accompany exhibitions, such as didactic panels, artists' or curatorial statements, branding, advertising or press statements
visiting and evaluating exhibitions of work in physical or virtual galleries, museums or in community sites
developing responses to exhibitions of work; for example, in written/oral/multimedia explanations or reviews
constructing explanations of how artists, designers, architects or craftspeople communicate ideas and meaning in artworks
